newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mostly firm as futures strengthen.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mostly firm as futures strengthen.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mostly stronger on Monday, traders said.

Gasoline was notionally firmer as NYMEX crude oil futures gained ground. The region remains tight. Turkey's Tupras said it had awarded a tender to buy 27,000 tonnes of gasoline on June 11-14 to Poten, and another tender to buy 25,000 tonnes of gasoline on June 6-8 from Vitol. The tenders were awarded at -$17.35 and also at -$17.50, based on fob Med quotes, but more precise information was not supplied by Tupras.
Tupras also sold 22,000 tonnes of naphtha to Poten, the company said. No more details were available.

Gas oil was a mixed bag. Low sulphur diesel strengthened as arbitrage opportunities to northwest Europe drained material out of the region leaving buyers high and dry. A major was reported to be scouting for material.
Many Mediterranean refineries appeared to have placed all their low sulphur material until the end of June, while the few Algerian cargoes on offer appeared to have gone northward.
Traders pegged low sulphur diesel prices around quotes fob hi +$2.0/+$3.0 a tonne.
Heating oil, meanwhile, remained on the sloppy side as large quantities of Russian material overhung the market.
Prices were pegged around quotes fob hi -$1.0/50 cents.

High sulphur fuel rose on better bunker demand and a lack of prompt Russian material, but some traders cautioned the rise was overdone. Med swaps at $77.50/$78 for June led the way, with physical $1 lower.
"Med swaps are up on the back of expectation of continued demand for arbitrage cargoes to take to the Far East or North America," said one trader, "but a lot of it is just hype."
An Italian high sulphur producer has already sold out June production and was seeing demand for July stocks from out of the region, an indication of keen interest in still cheap fuel.
